title: Engagement Origami — QBR preflight, adaptable agenda, and facilitation script
content:
Purpose: A compact, modular QBR facilitation and preflight checklist designed to let Customer Success teams quickly assemble a meeting agenda tailored to the audience (executive, product, technical), highlight renewal signals, and leave with a clear set of owner-assigned next steps.

Document overview (how to use):
- 'Origami' concept: build the QBR by folding in/out modules. Each module is ~10–20 minutes and can be swapped depending on time and attendees.
- Use the preflight checklist (section A) 48–72 hours before the meeting.
- Print the one-page facilitation cheat (section B) for the facilitator.
- After the QBR, run the follow-up template (section E) within 24 hours.

A. Preflight checklist (48–72h window) — task owner and verification
1) Account context snapshot (owner: CSM) — include current ARR, contract renewal date, last invoiced, core product modules in use, critical integrations. (Attach CSV or screenshot from CRM).
2) Usage & health highlights (owner: Data Ops / CSM) — 7/30/90 day active seats, API calls per minute, top 5 latency or error trends, support ticket counts last 90 days. Minimal table expected: metric | period | trend | note.
3) Product changes & roadmap items (owner: Solutions Engineer) — list items affecting the customer, with release dates and risk impact (none/low/medium/high).
4) Customer wins & friction points (owner: CSM) — collate two bullets for wins, two for friction/unresolved blockers.
5) Renewal posture & signals (owner: CSM + Rev Ops) — current renewal probability estimate (Low/Med/High), expansion opportunity (yes/no + $ est), legal/compliance blockers, procurement timeline.
6) Stakeholder mapping & meeting invite sanity check (owner: CSM) — confirm attendees and primary objectives per attendee (execs want outcomes, engineers want technical deep dive).
7) Slide deck + pre-read (owner: CSM) — prepare 1 slide per module, attach 1–2 page pre-read summary for execs. Send pre-read 48 hours prior.
8) Facilitation logistics (owner: CSM) — dial-in link, recording permission, notetaker, and a confirmed follow-up owner.

B. Modular agenda (90-minute baseline, collapse to 30m/60m by removing modules)
- Opening (5m) — facilitator: brief objective, desired decisions, and timebox rules. Script: "Thanks everyone — objective is to align on health, blockers, and renewal actions. We’ll use a modular agenda; ask for clarifying questions at any time and capture action owners at the end."
- Executive pulse (10m) — 3-slide summary: ARR & topline usage trend, renewal posture + ask, 1 customer story. Facilitator script: "High-level numbers, likely renewal outcome, and the main ask we need a decision on today."
- Health deep-dive (15m) — product performance and adoption signals. Include 30/90 day cohorts and any latency/error anomalies. Facilitator script: "We’ll highlight three adoption signals we track and one risk signal we want help resolving."
- Roadmap impact & mitigations (10m) — product team explains any upcoming changes that affect the account. Ask: accept timeline or require mitigation plan.
- Use-case spotlight (15m) — customer presents one primary use-case; CS/SE present value realized. Goal: surface unmet needs and potential expansion.
- Risk triage & decision run (15m) — open issues prioritized; capture owners, deadlines, and escalation paths. Facilitator script: "For each item we’ll confirm owner, deadline, and what success looks like — if we can’t resolve here, we escalate to X."
- Commercial review & renewal ask (10m) — present recommended renewal terms, any concessions, and next steps. Ask: confirm Go/No-Go or timing for decision.
- Wrap & next steps (5m) — review action list and confirm communication cadence.

C. Facilitation cheat (one page — keep this on your tablet):
- Start by naming the decision: "Renewal timeline + scope of contract for FY26"
- Meeting norms: timebox, hand-raising for deep dives, parking lot for tech demos.
- Quick triage questions (if conversation stalls): Who needs more info to decide? What data/attachment will resolve this?
- Escalation ladder: CSM -> Solutions Lead -> Director CS -> Head of Rev Ops (list emails/handles).
- Notetaker cue: capture (1) decision, (2) owner, (3) due date, (4) blocker.

D. Red flags and renewal triggers (operationalizable signals)
- Usage drop: >25% MoM reduction in active users in two consecutive weeks.
- Support spike: >3 severity-1/2 incidents in 30 days without resolution.
- Unaddressed product blocker: open engineering ticket >45 days with customer impact.
- Procurement stalling: no PO or contract signature within 30 days of verbal commitment.
- Positive expansion trigger: consistent >10% QoQ growth in feature adoption or new paid seats >5 in quarter.

E. Post-meeting follow-up template (send within 24 hours) — subject and body skeleton
Subject: [Account] QBR recap — decisions & owners (date)
Body: Hi <Stakeholders>,
Thanks for your time. Quick recap:
- Decision(s) made: 1) <short decision> — Owner: <name> — Due: <date>
- Open items: 1) <item> — Owner: <name> — Due: <date>
- Risk signals flagged: <list>
- Commercial next step: <renewal proposal sent/negotiation/PO pending>
Attachments: pre-read, slide deck, action tracker link
Please flag any inaccuracies within 48 hours. If no reply, we’ll assume actions are accurate and proceed.
Best,
<CSM name>

F. Action tracker (minimal columns for CRM / sheet ingestion)
- Columns expected: account_id | owner | action_item | due_date | status | context_link | priority | escalated_to
Example row: 12345 | Maya S. | Resolve API timeout for endpoint X | 2026-03-05 | in_progress | https://github.com/redwood/ticket/456 | high | Eng-Lead

G. Customizable scripts (pick depending on audience)
1) Exec-level script (concise): "We’ll cover overall health, two risks that could impact the contract, and the renewal ask. Looking for alignment on the proposed commercial terms today."
2) Tech-level script (detailed): "We’ll spend 15 minutes on a technical run of errors and root-cause options — please bring your SRE/infra contact."
3) Product partner script (growth focus): "We’ll review three adoption signals and solicit agreement on an experiment to increase adoption of feature Y."

H. Templates / artifacts to attach to the meeting invite
- 2-page pre-read (topline metrics + 3 asks)
- Action tracker sheet (editable; link in invite)
- Relevant support ticket list export (CSV)
- Proposed renewal term sheet (PDF)

I. Quick facilitation heuristics and pitfalls to avoid
- Don’t bury the renewal ask in a long technical demo — call it out early.
- Watch for silent execs — call them out and ask for a thumbs-up or one-line view.
- Avoid technical rabbit holes unless technical owners are present — capture and schedule a follow-up deep dive.
- If multiple stakeholders disagree, surface trade-offs and propose a time-limited pilot to buy decision velocity.

J. Example 'decision capture' line (copy-paste to notes):
Decision: Renew FY26 at $X with standard terms. Owner: Head of Procurement (Acme) — Due: 2026-05-12 — Conditions: Product GAP 2 addressed by 2026-04-30, engineering runbook delivered.

K. Quick reference: meeting lengths and which modules to keep
- 30 min (exec-only): Opening, Executive pulse, Commercial review & renewal ask, Wrap
- 60 min (standard): Opening, Executive pulse, Health deep-dive, Roadmap impact, Commercial review & renewal ask, Wrap
- 90 min (full): All modules + Use-case spotlight + Risk triage

L. Ownership convention: initials only in tracker for speed (e.g., MS = Maya Singh). Always include full name in follow-up emails.

M. Version control & feedback
- Filename convention: account-YYYYMMDD-engagement-origami-vX.docx
- Please leave comments in the shared doc for improvements — this is intended as an evolving playbook.

Last checklist before sending pre-read (15m):
- Remove slides that are not relevant to present audience
- Confirm notetaker and whether recording is OK
- Attach action tracker and pre-read
- Quick sanity check: does the deck surface the exact ‘ask’? If not — fix.

Notes and open questions to iterate in future versions:
- Add a one-click renewal scoring widget for CS console exports.
- Standardize 3 adoption signals across product lines so CS teams speak the same language.
- Explore an automated preflight pipeline that scrapes CRM and product metrics to populate the pre-read.

End of document.
